name: Kraków
tagline: Poland's former royal capital, with Europe's largest medieval market square, a hilltop castle, a historic Jewish quarter and a salt mine of underground chapels.
highlight: The Main Market Square at dusk, with the trumpeter's call from St. Mary's tower and horse carriages passing the Cloth Hall.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed old town with the Main Market Square, Wawel Castle, Kazimierz, Schindler's Factory and easy trips to Wieliczka Salt Mine and Auschwitz.
metaDescription: A Kraków travel guide: Main Market Square, Cloth Hall, Wawel Castle, St. Mary's Basilica, Kazimierz, Wieliczka Salt Mine, food, where to stay, how to get around and a three-day plan.

image.alt: The Cloth Hall in Kraków's Main Market Square

intro: Kraków is Poland's most visited city and its cultural capital, home to about 800,000 people, and it was the seat of the Polish kings for five centuries. Unlike Warsaw, it escaped major destruction in the Second World War, so its medieval old town, ringed by the Planty park where the walls once stood, is intact, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1978.

At the centre is the Main Market Square, the largest medieval town square in Europe, with the Renaissance Cloth Hall in the middle and St. Mary's Basilica at one corner, from whose tower a trumpeter plays a call every hour. To the south, Wawel Hill holds the royal castle and cathedral. Further south is Kazimierz, the historic Jewish quarter, now full of restored synagogues, cafés and bars, and across the river is Podgórze, with the Schindler's Factory museum.

Kraków is also the base for two major excursions: the Wieliczka Salt Mine, a UNESCO-listed complex of chambers and chapels carved from salt, and Auschwitz-Birkenau. It has a vibrant student life, and its cellar bars and restaurants are excellent value. Three days covers the city, with more for excursions.

whyVisit.intro: Kraków is Poland's most complete and atmospheric historic city.

attractionsIntro: The old town is compact and best on foot.

attractions.name: Main Market Square and the Cloth Hall

image.file: File:Krakow 2024 032 St Mary Basilica et Sukiennice Mascarons.jpg
image.alt: St. Mary's Basilica beside the Cloth Hall in Kraków's Main Market Square

attractions.text: The largest medieval square in Europe, with the Renaissance Cloth Hall trading arcade, the town hall tower and St. Mary's Basilica with its altarpiece by Veit Stoss.
attractions.tip: Listen for the hourly trumpet call.

attractions.name: Wawel Castle and Cathedral

image.alt: Wawel Hill with the castle and cathedral rising above the Vistula

attractions.text: The seat of Polish kings for centuries, with a Renaissance courtyard, state rooms and a cathedral where monarchs were crowned and buried.

attractions.name: Kazimierz

image.file: File:Józefa Street, view from E, Kazimierz, Kraków, Poland.jpg
image.alt: Józefa Street in the Kazimierz district of Kraków

attractions.text: The historic Jewish quarter, with synagogues, a lively square and many bars and restaurants, and a serious past to remember.

attractions.name: Wieliczka Salt Mine

image.file: File:202207 Holy Cross Chapel in Wieliczka Salt Mine 01.jpg
image.alt: The Holy Cross Chapel carved from salt in the Wieliczka Salt Mine

attractions.text: A UNESCO-listed mine 14 km from the city, worked since the Middle Ages, with chapels and statues carved from rock salt.
attractions.tip: Allow half a day, and dress warmly.

attractions.name: Schindler's Factory
attractions.text: A museum about Kraków under Nazi occupation, in Oskar Schindler's former enamel factory.

attractions.name: Planty Park
attractions.text: A green ring around the old town, on the site of the medieval walls.

thingsToDo.title: Climb the St. Mary's tower
thingsToDo.text: See the trumpeter and the square.

foodIntro: Kraków's food is hearty and cheap.

foods.name: Obwarzanek
foods.text: A boiled and baked bread ring.

foods.name: Zapiekanka
foods.text: A toasted baguette pizza from Plac Nowy.

accommodation.intro: Stay in or near the old town.

bestTime.headline: May–September
bestTime.summary: Kraków has warm summers and cold winters.

itinerary.title: Three days in Kraków
itinerary.intro: The old town, Kazimierz, and a salt mine.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you plan.
tips: Book Wawel, Wieliczka and Schindler's Factory in advance.
Go to the square early or late.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Kraków?
faq.a: Three days, with more for excursions.

faq.q: Can I visit Auschwitz from Kraków?

faq.a: Its old town, castle and Jewish heritage.
